title: A bot that took zero trades can still tell you something useful
author: Electrical_Waltz_888
selftext:
Say you paper trade a bot for a week and it never enters. Did no setups qualify? Was the data stale? Did the system never get far enough to check?

“Zero trades” looks identical in the P&L report for all three. The next step is different in each case.

I’d log one reason every time the bot evaluates a setup: **no signal**, **signal blocked**, **order rejected**, or **order accepted**. I’d also record missed evaluations separately, so a scheduler that didn’t run can’t look like a strategy that was patiently waiting.

Then I’d give AI the log and ask: “Which sessions confirm that the strategy ran and found no setup? Which show a system problem? Which can’t be explained from the records?”

Before changing the entry rules to get more trades, I’d want to know whether those rules were actually evaluated.

If your bot sits idle all week, what’s the first thing you check?

Disclosure: I wrote *The Complete Guide to AI Powered Trading* . It includes worked examples and 50 reusable prompts for writing trading rules, questioning backtest results and reviewing trades with AI.
